title: Ultra-processed foods, lifestyle management, and cardiovascular diseases: a clinical consensus statement of the European Society of Cardiology Council for Cardiology Practice and the European Association of Preventive Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
authors: Guasti L, Bonaccio M, Abreu A, Asteggiano R, Bes-Rastrollo M, Christodorescu R, et al.
authorConflicts: Disclosure of interest: nothing to declare.
result: Associations of ultra-processed food intake with cardiovascular risk factors, incidence and mortality derive predominantly from observational studies, to be interpreted with caution because residual confounding and reverse causation cannot be fully excluded; trials are scarce, short-term and limited to surrogate outcomes, and trials of reduced intake on hard cardiovascular endpoints are lacking. Proposed non-nutrient mechanisms (additives, processing contaminants, packaging migrants, altered food matrix) support biological plausibility without demonstrating causal effects. General cardiologists are advised to assess intake of ultra-processed food and include it in counselling.
